# Minimal reading-order controls

Synthetic PDFs generated by `scripts/probe-reader-font-order.py` using pypdf
6.14.2. No private documents or embedded third-party fonts. All use standard
Courier, source text `ABCDEF`, and `/Rotate 180`.

- `single-180.pdf`: one TJ operation; raw PDFium copies `ABCDEF`.
- `split-180.pdf`: three adjacent same-font TJ operations; raw PDFium copies
  `EF CD AB`. Font switching and Type3 are not required for the defect.
- `counterrotated-180.pdf`: three TJ operations with a negative text matrix;
  raw PDFium correctly copies `ABCDEF`. Unconditional rotation removal breaks it.

SHA-256:

```text
976ab3ce619ced4a8792d1a8c56f97ffb82edf190fa85219a6504c3aa7e62296  single-180.pdf
e8ccb62041c6cf58d28a1468746bbeaeccd795801af26d8d11f510f37a2733a3  split-180.pdf
8180f918d5ad490c8629ca6c45193dba9927a7b1cab77185c1ae9fe66505da9b  counterrotated-180.pdf
```

The complete raw matrices and reader versions are recorded in
`docs/reader-order-minimal.json` and `docs/reader-order-counterrotation.json`.
These files are regression controls for Folio's bounded reader workaround,
not a claim that raw PDFium or portable complex-text serialization is fixed.
